newsitem.title: FRANCE: France says Britain admits dumping offer illegal.
newsitem.headline: France says Britain admits dumping offer illegal.

text.p: France said on Wednesday Britain had confirmed that an offer by a British company to sub-contract staff to French companies to avoid paying France's higher social charges was illegal.

European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier in a statement quoted the British ambassador in Paris, Michael Jay, as writing to him that "the activity offered by this company is illegal under British law".

Hotel and Catering Staff Supplies Ltd of Rotherham, England, insisting the proposal is legal, is offering to recruit seasonal employees for hotels and restaurants in other European Union countries with the prospect of paying up to 30 percent less in payroll deductions.

Workers on six-month contracts would pay British national insurance contributions but would be entitled to full reciprocal coverage by the French public health service while employed in France, it said.
Barnier, accusing he company of "social dumping", has said his ministry's legal department had concluded that such contracts would breach both French and EU law.
He said detaching foreign workers to France could only be done under strict regulations.

He quoted Jay as writing: "I can assure you that the British government is determined to fight such breaches of provisions intended to facilitate free movement of workers between European Union member countries."
The director of the British firm, Charles Rhodes, has said his system was a cheaper way for French hotels to recruit British staff to serve their English-speaking clientele and was entirely legal.
